spec: Find the maximum word length in the non-empty list words, then return a sorted list of all words that have that maximum length (there may be one or several).
Find the minimum word length in the non-empty list words, then return a sorted list of all words that have that minimum length (there may be one or several).
Return a sorted list of the keys that are present in all three dicts d1, d2, and d3. If there is no such key, return an empty list.
Given a dict, count how many keys map to each distinct value. Return a dict mapping each distinct value found in d to the number of keys that have it. An empty dict returns an empty dict.
Given two lists of the same length, count the number of positions at which the elements are equal. Return that count as an integer. Two empty lists return 0.

Consider only the words in the list that have length at least prefix_len, and take the first prefix_len characters of each as its prefix. Count how many words share each such prefix. Return a dict mapping each occupied prefix to its count. If no word is long enough, or the list is empty, return an empty dict.

Bucket each non-negative integer score into a decade label: '0-9', '10-19', ..., '90-99', or '100+' for scores of 100 and above. Return a dict mapping each label with at least one score to its count (labels with no scores are omitted). An empty list returns an empty dict.
Given a dict with string keys, count how many keys have each possible key length. Return a dict mapping each key length to the number of keys of that length. An empty dict returns an empty dict.

Combine the keys of three numeric dicts d1, d2, d3. For each key present in any of them, sum the values from every dict that has it (treating a missing key as 0). Return the resulting dict. Three empty dicts return an empty dict.

Given a dict with numeric values, split its keys into two groups: those whose value falls within [low, high] inclusive ('in_range'), and all others ('out_range'). Return a dict with keys 'in_range' and 'out_range' each mapping to a sorted list of the matching dict keys.

For every key that appears in either numeric dict d1 or d2, compute the average of the values present for that key (using just one value if the key appears in only one dict). Return a dict mapping each key to that average (a float). Two empty dicts return an empty dict.

Reconstruct a nested dict from a flat dict whose keys encode a path joined by the given separator string. For each entry, split the key on the separator and build (or reuse) nested dicts for every path segment except the last, then set the final segment to the value. An empty input dict returns an empty dict.

Flatten a nested dict into a single-level dict whose keys are tuples recording the full path of original keys. A value that is a non-empty dict is recursed into, extending the path tuple; any other value (including an empty dict) becomes a leaf under its path tuple. An empty input dict returns an empty dict.

Reconstruct a nested dict from a flat dict whose keys are tuples describing a path of nested keys. For each entry, walk (or create) nested dicts for every path element except the last, then set the final element to the value. An empty input dict returns an empty dict.

Safely look up a value inside a nested dict using a dotted (or otherwise separator-joined) path string. Split the path on the separator and descend one key at a time; if at any step the current value is not a dict or does not contain the next key, return the given default value instead of raising an error.

Return a new nested dict equal to d but with the value at the given separator-joined path set to value, creating any missing intermediate dicts along the way (overwriting a non-dict value found in the middle of the path with an empty dict before continuing). The original dict d must not be mutated.

Recursively merge two nested dicts a and b. When a key exists in both and both values are dicts, merge them recursively. When a key exists in both and both values are numbers (int or float, not bool), sum them. Otherwise the value from b is used (including for keys only present in one of the two). Two empty dicts return an empty dict.

Merge a list of flat dicts into a single dict, prefixing each original key with its record's position in the list (0-based) and a dot, e.g. record 0's key 'name' becomes '0.name'. This keeps every key unique even if the same key name occurs in several records. An empty list returns an empty dict.

Given two dicts of numbers, old and new, compare the value of every key that appears in both. Return a dict mapping each such common key to the string 'increased' if the new value is larger, 'decreased' if it is smaller, or 'same' if they are equal. Keys not present in both dicts are ignored entirely.

Given a list of dicts, return a sorted list of the keys that are present in every one of them. If the list is empty, return an empty list. If the list has a single dict, return all of its keys sorted.

Given a list of dicts, return a sorted list of the keys that appear in exactly one of the dicts in the list (counting a key once per dict it appears in, regardless of value). An empty list, or one where every key repeats across dicts, returns an empty list.
Return a sorted list of the keys that appear in exactly one of the two given dicts a and b (not both). If a and b have identical key sets, or both are empty, return an empty list.

Given two dicts a and b, return a dict containing only the keys present in both, mapping each such key to a tuple of (a's value, b's value). Keys unique to either dict are excluded. If there are no common keys, or either dict is empty, return an empty dict.

Return a new dict containing only the entries of d whose numeric value falls within the inclusive range [low, high]. The original dict is left unmodified. If nothing qualifies, or d is empty, return an empty dict.

Return a new dict containing only the entries of d whose integer value is even. The original dict is left unmodified. Negative even numbers count as even. If nothing qualifies, or d is empty, return an empty dict.

Return a new dict keeping only the entries of d whose string key starts with the given prefix AND whose value is greater than or equal to min_value. Both conditions must hold. If nothing qualifies, or d is empty, return an empty dict.

Return a list of (key, value) tuples for the k entries of d with the largest values, ordered by value descending and, for ties, by key ascending. If k exceeds the number of entries, return all of them in that order. If k is 0 or d is empty, return an empty list.

Given a dict of numeric values, rank the keys by value descending using standard competition ('1224') ranking: the largest value gets rank 1, tied keys share the same rank, and the next distinct value's rank is its 1-based position in the descending order (so ties cause the following rank to be skipped). Return a dict mapping each key to its integer rank. An empty dict returns an empty dict.

Given a dict of numeric values, rank the keys by value descending using dense ranking: the largest value gets rank 1, tied keys share the same rank, and the next distinct (smaller) value gets the very next consecutive rank (no ranks are skipped for ties). Return a dict mapping each key to its integer rank. An empty dict returns an empty dict.

Return the second-highest distinct value found among d's values (i.e. the largest value that is strictly less than the maximum). If d has fewer than two distinct values (including an empty dict, or a dict where every value is the same), return None.
Return the difference between the largest and smallest value in d (max minus min). An empty dict, or a dict with a single entry, returns 0.

Given a list of words, count how often each consecutive triple of words (a trigram) occurs, using a tuple of the three words as the key. Return a dict mapping each trigram tuple to its count. A list with fewer than three words returns an empty dict.

Given a string s, count how often each pair of adjacent characters occurs, using the two-character substring as the key. Return a dict mapping each bigram string to its count. A string with fewer than two characters returns an empty dict.

Given a dict with string keys and numeric values, merge entries whose keys are equal when compared case-insensitively, summing their values, and use the lowercase form of the key in the result. Return the merged dict. An empty dict returns an empty dict.

Given a list of 2-element tuples of comparable values, count how often each unordered pair occurs, treating (a, b) as the same pair as (b, a). Use a tuple with the smaller element first (or either, if equal) as the key. Return a dict mapping each canonical pair tuple to its count. An empty list returns an empty dict.
Given a non-empty list of 2-element tuples, find the tuple that occurs most often. If several tuples are tied for the highest count, return the lexicographically smallest of them. Return that tuple.
Given a dict, count how many keys map to each distinct value. Return a dict mapping each distinct value found in d to the number of keys that have it. An empty dict returns an empty dict.
Given a dict mapping items to their occurrence counts, return a sorted list of the items whose count is exactly 1. An empty dict, or one with no such items, returns an empty list.
Given a dict mapping items to their occurrence counts, return a sorted list of the items whose count is greater than 1. An empty dict, or one where every item occurs once, returns an empty list.

Given a list of integers, count how often each decimal digit (0-9) occurs across all of their absolute values written out in base 10. Return a dict mapping each digit character that occurs to its total count. An empty list returns an empty dict.
